cycles.summary: Finished an unfinished skill package -- a parallel worker had authored a complete, high-quality SKILL.md (8 instruction steps, 3 worked examples, gotchas, reference links, troubleshooting) but timed out before adding the supporting files. This cycle added SKILL_HE.md, two reference docs (diligence-checklist.md, red-flag-clauses.md), the stdlib-only diligence_scanner.py script, and metadata/evidence/optimization-log JSON. Fixed a regex bug found during self-test: the data_breach_indemnity pattern used a {0,60} character window that failed on the multi-line selftest fixture because raw text wasn't whitespace-normalized before matching; fixed by normalizing all whitespace to single spaces before scanning (also more robust against real-world contract line wrapping).

changes.detail: Added SKILL_HE.md: Hebrew mirror of the 8-step framework, gotchas, and reference links.
Added references/diligence-checklist.md (scored checklist across 5 areas + risk tiering) and references/red-flag-clauses.md (12-row red-flag catalogue with fix/ask).

Added scripts/diligence_scanner.py: regex-based coverage scan across 10 clause types (breach notification, DPA/sub-processors, liability cap, breach carve-out, SLA/credits, chronic-failure termination, data return/deletion, auto-renewal, IP indemnity, data-breach indemnity) plus a keyword-based risk-tier hint.

Selftest initially failed on data_breach_indemnity due to a {0,60}/{0,100} char-window regex not matching across a wrapped multi-line fixture. Root cause: no whitespace normalization before matching. Fixed by re.sub(whitespace->single-space) at the top of scan(), which also makes the scanner robust to real contract line-wrap/PDF-extraction artifacts.
Added metadata.json (bilingual tags/display, supported agents) and evidence.json (5 claims sourced to NIST SP 800-161, GDPR Art. 28, CSA STAR, plus the local script self-check).

deferrals.reason: The scanner reports clause presence/absence by regex pattern only; it cannot judge whether a present clause is adequate (e.g. a cap that exists but is set too low). This is documented as a Gotcha and in the script's module docstring rather than solved, since adequacy judgment requires reading the actual clause text, not pattern matching.
